title: Game Boy Advance
wiki_lead:
The Game Boy Advance (GBA) is a handheld game console developed and marketed by Nintendo, which was released in Japan on March 21, 2001, and in other regions in June. It was later released in mainland China in 2004, under the name iQue Game Boy Advance. Compared to the Game Boy Color it succeeded, the console offered a significantly more powerful ARM7 processor and improved graphics, while retaining backward compatibility with games initially developed for its predecessor.
The 32-bit GBA is part of the sixth generation of video game consoles, competing against Nokia's N-Gage and Bandai's Japan-only WonderSwan. The original model was followed in 2003 by the Game Boy Advance SP, a redesigned model with a frontlit screen and clamshell form factor. A newer revision of the SP with a backlit screen was released in 2005. A miniaturized redesign, the Game Boy Micro, was released in September 2005.
By June 2010, the Game Boy Advance series including revisions, had sold 81.51 million units worldwide, massively outselling its competitors. Its successor, the Nintendo DS, launched on November 21, 2004, was backward compatible with GBA games. GBA sales ended by 2010 after over nine years.
In 2008, the GBA was still Nintendo's predominant handheld console in terms of market presence and global installed base. It was only in late October 2008 that Nintendo announced that the Nintendo DS had officially surpassed the GBA worldwide in sales. This milestone consolidated the definitive global leadership transition between generations, although in specific markets, such as the United States, the GBA was only surpassed by the Nintendo DS in sales in late 2009.

History


Project Atlantis
When the original Game Boy launched in 1989, many questioned Nintendo's decision to release a monochrome handheld console, when competitors like the Lynx and Game Gear had color screens. However, the rivals' color displays were criticized for their poor battery life and bulky size, while the Game Boy's better portability and battery longevity increased its popularity.
Nintendo publicly pledged to develop a color version of the Game Boy only when the technology overcame the limitations of existing color handhelds. Internally, however, a team led by Satoru Okada—who had worked on the original Game Boy—was already experimenting with color screens. Their early 1990s prototype, codenamed "Project Atlantis," featured a color display and a 32-bit processor designed by ARM. Despite the promising technology, the team was not satisfied with the outcome and the project was shelved by 1997.
However, as competitors such as the Neo Geo Pocket and WonderSwan entered the market, Nintendo decided to create a color version of the Game Boy by combining the color screen they had been testing for Project Atlantis with a faster version of the existing Game Boy's 8-bit processor. The Game Boy Color launched in 1998.

grok_lead: The Game Boy Advance (GBA) is a 32-bit handheld video game console developed, published, and marketed by Nintendo as the successor to the Game Boy Color in the sixth generation of video game consoles. It was released in Japan on March 21, 2001, in North America on June 11, 2001, and in Europe and Australia on June 22, 2001. Featuring a redesigned ergonomic form factor with dimensions of 82 mm Ã 144.5 mm Ã 24.5 mm and a weight of 140 grams, the GBA introduced a larger 2.9-inch TFT reflective LCD screen with a 240 Ã 160 pixel resolution capable of displaying up to 32,768 colors. Powered by a 32-bit ARM7TDMI processor running at 16.8 MHz, it included 32 KB of internal RAM, 96 KB of video RAM, and 256 KB of external work RAM, enabling more advanced graphics and sound compared to prior Game Boy systems. The console supported backward compatibility with original Game Boy and Game Boy Color game cartridges, while its native games utilized enhanced 32-bit architecture for titles resembling Super Nintendo Entertainment System-level experiences in a portable format. It offered approximately 15 hours of gameplay on two AA alkaline batteries, a built-in speaker, a headphone jack for stereo PCM audio, and connectivity options including a link cable for multiplayer and integration with the Nintendo GameCube via a special cable for data transfer and controller use. The GBA achieved massive commercial success, with lifetime worldwide sales exceeding 81.51 million units, establishing it as Nintendo's third best-selling handheld console after the Nintendo DS and the combined original Game Boy family. Over 1,000 games have been released for the system as of 2025, including landmark titles such as Super Mario Advance, The Legend of Zelda: The Minish Cap, PokÃ©mon Ruby and Sapphire, Metroid Fusion, Metroid: Zero Mission, Advance Wars, Castlevania: Aria of Sorrow, and Final Fantasy Tactics Advance, which showcased its capabilities and contributed to its enduring popularity; support continued with the release of Shantae Advance: Risky Revolution in April 2025. Nintendo later introduced variants to address user feedback, including the clamshell-designed Game Boy Advance SP in 2003 with a front-lit screen and rechargeable battery, and the pocket-sized Game Boy Micro in 2005, extending the platform's lifecycle even as the Nintendo DS began succeeding it in 2004. The GBA's innovations in portable gaming, combining power, portability, and broad compatibility, solidified its legacy as a pivotal device in the evolution of handheld entertainment.
